# Synthetic-data caveat

These two onboarding acceptance fixtures are explicitly synthetic workflow checks and do not describe real researcher behaviour or validated usability findings, so any pain points and improvements discussed here should be treated as design hypotheses rather than evidence from actual users.[1] [2]

# Observed navigation and clarity pain points (synthetic fixtures)

Within projects, both fixtures describe confusion about where uploads land and what a “project” or “mission” actually is, including uncertainty over whether importing notes starts a paid run, which project receives the file, and whether a project is an empty folder, an active research job, or something else.[1] [2] Both synthetic researchers struggle to locate the correct entry point for uploads, moving between project pages and document lists, and wanting clearer destination labels, confirmations naming the project and document, and persistent display of the current project near upload actions.[1] [2] They also report difficulty distinguishing projects, collections, and Spaces, worrying that saving excerpts might move originals, asking for previews that show collection names, destinations, sources, and selected excerpts, and expecting navigation away to sources and back not to discard in-progress collection setup or make it unclear which similarly named collection to continue.[1] [2]

# Recommendations derived from these fixtures (not real findings)

To address these synthetic pain points, the workflow could show explicit, persistent destination indicators beside upload and save actions, provide short inline explanations of what uploads and collections do and do not change, and use confirmations that clearly name the target project, collection, and included excerpts to reduce ambiguity about where material is going.[1] [2] Collections and reports could maintain stable previews that do not regenerate on save, preserve reviewed names and membership across navigation, and expose links back to excerpt-level context without moving documents or silently renaming existing structures.[1] [2] When saves are interrupted, the interface might offer a structured retry path that surfaces any already-created collection, highlights which excerpts or passages are missing, and clarifies which subset of materials is eligible for analysis, while avoiding autonomous background organisation or permission changes that neither synthetic fixture requested.[1] [2]
